successors.name: Haudenosaunee Confederacy
successors.text: Wendake, the Wendat homeland 'between Georgian Bay and Lake Simcoe' (the discs are the researcher's reading)

ledger.x: 15th century: the Wendat confederacy forms between Georgian Bay and Lake Simcoe.
c. 1590: the Arendarhonon (Arendaenronnon) join. 'The Arendaenronnon joined about 1590'; Atironta, their headman, 'went to Quebec and allied with the French in 1609'. The page names no tract.
c. 1610: the Atahontaenrat (Tahontaenrat) join as the fourth nation. 'The Atahontaenrat joined around 1610'; the Ataronchronon 'may not have attained full membership'. The page names no tract.
1649: the fighting for Wendake ends with the homeland empty; the Iroquois page: the League 'defeated and assimilated most of the Huron (1649)'.
1649: the Wendat Confederacy loses its homeland.

wars.name: Beaver Wars (Wendat campaign)
wars.outcome: The Haudenosaunee destroyed Wendake in 1649; about 10,000 Wendat fled to Christian Island, where most starved, and the survivors dispersed to Quebec, the Petun and the upper Great Lakes.

certainty.note: The homeland is known by the villages' archaeology and by the pages' 'between Georgian Bay and Lake Simcoe'; no frontier is given.
